---
title: "Adapting the pipeline for other HPC systems"
author: "Caitlin Cherryh"
date: "2025-05-02"
output: html_document
---

This pipeline was developed for use on the CSIRO HPC system Petrichor.

Some choices were made to make running the pipeline on this system easy and 
adaptable for users. For example, users specify the environment modules in the
`chromatin_assembly_config.yml` file. This allows the version of the module used
in the pipeline to be updated as the system is updated. On the down side,
it means commands to load environment modules are hardcoded in the shell commands
for individual rules, rather than being defined within the rule using the 
`envmodules:` command.

These choices mean some modifications are necessary to run the pipeline on 
an alternative HPC system.

There are two main ways to update the pipeline for your HPC system.

-----

## Using environment modules
If your HPC system uses an environment module system, you should be able to 
simply update the names of the environment modules within the 
`chromatin_assembly_config.yml` file.

The modules used (as of 17/04/2025) are:
```
##### Section 5: Modules #####
# Update module versions here, as required
modules:
  danpos: "danpos/3.1.1"
  fastqc: "fastqc/0.11.9"
  fgbio: "fgbio/2.0.2"
  kit4b: "kit4b/200218"
  picard: "picard/3.0.0"
  python: "python/3.9.4"
  R: "R/4.0.5"
  repeatmasker: "repeatmasker/4.1.2p1"
  samtools: "samtools/1.18.0"
```

For example, if the DANPOS module in your HPC system is called `DANPOS` and is v3.0.0, you would
update the name as such:
```
##### Section 5: Modules #####
# Update module versions here, as required
modules:
  danpos: "DANPOS/3.0.0"
```

Step 6 of the pipeline also uses the programs faToTwoBit, twoBitInfo, 
and faCount. These are accessed within the pipeline when Step 6 is executed,
using the provided conda environment `workflow/envs/Step6_utils.yaml`. Provided
the HPC system you are using has conda environments, you will not need to do
anything to make this work.

-----

## Using conda environments

> Important:
> This approach has not been tested.

If your HPC does not have environment modules, or you wish to use a conda 
environment for some other reason, I provide a version of the pipeline that uses
a conda environment with the majority of software packages. The conda environment
does not need to be specified by the user, as it is included in the conda-only 
Snakefile.

### Key differences

In the original pipeline, the following steps are executed using the `kit4b` module:

- Step 1: creating suffix array (after RepeatMasker is applied to reference genome) with `ngskit4b index`
- Step 4: read alignment with `ngskit4b kalign`

The kit4b module is no longer available. For the conda environment version of the
pipeline, we recommend installing [biokanga](https://github.com/csiro-crop-informatics/biokanga).

The shell commands for these steps have been updated to use 
[biokanga](https://github.com/csiro-crop-informatics/biokanga):

- Step 1: `ngskit4b index` replaced with `biokanga index`
- Step 4: `ngskit4b kalign` replaced with `biokanga align`

### Software installation
Before running the conda-only version of the pipeline, you will also need to 
install:

- [biokanga](https://github.com/csiro-crop-informatics/biokanga)
- [DANPOS3](https://github.com/sklasfeld/DANPOS3)

You may need to:

- update the shell command for Step 1 and Step 4 to ensure the path to biokanga is correct for your installation
- update the shell command for Step 8 to ensure the path to DANPOS3 is correct for your installation


### Running the conda-only version
There is a separate Snakefile and config file for this version.

The config file is at `workflow/conda_only_version/chromatin_assembly_config.yml`.
Follow the instructions in the quick-start guide `README.md` to enter parameters
for your dataset.

The Snakefile is at `workflow/conda_only_version/Snakefile`

If you use this version, you will need to add the following flags to Snakemake 
calls:

- Specify the conda-only version of the Snakefile with `--snakefile`
- Specify the conda-only version of the config file with `--configfile`
- Tell Snakemake to use conda environments with `--use-conda`

```
snakemake \
  --use-conda  \
  --snakefile workflow/conda_only_version/Snakefile \
  --configfile workflow/conda_only_version/chromatin_assembly_config.yml 
```

Other arguments are added as usual.
e.g., to perform a dry run:
```
snakemake \
  --use-conda \
  --snakefile workflow/conda_only_version/Snakefile \
  --configfile workflow/conda_only_version/chromatin_assembly_config.yml \
  -c1 -n -p
```

If you are using the provided jobscripts, remember to update the Snakemake call 
within each jobscript.
